'''Rhonda M. Stroud''' (born 1971){{r|sbdb}} is a [[materials science|materials physicist]] and [[planetary science|planetary scientist]] at [[Arizona State University]], where she serves as Director of the Buseck Center for Meteorite Studies.{{r|BCMS}}  From 1998- 2022, she was a Research Physicist at the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory]], where she led the Nanoscale Materials Section.{{r|asteroid}} She is known for her research on [[nanostructure]]s, including [[quasicrystal]]s and [[aerogel]],{{r|fellow}} and on the materials that make up [[comet]]s{{r|comet}} and [[cosmic dust]].{{r|dust|interstellar}} She pioneered the use of [[focused ion beam]] technology in the study of [[meteorites]].{{r|FIB}}

==Education and career==
Stroud graduated from [[Cornell University]] in 1991 and completed a Ph.D. in 1996 at [[Washington University in St. Louis]].{{r|fellow}} She joined the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory|Naval Research Laboratory]] in 1996 as a postdoctoral researcher, and two years later obtained a permanent position there as a Research Physicist.{{r|visible}}

She served as president of the Microanalysis Society for 2018–2020.{{r|mas}}

==Recognition==
Stroud was elected as a [[List of American Physical Society Fellows (1998–2010)|Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2010, {{r|fellow}} of the [[Microscopy Society of America]] in 2021.,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.microscopy.org/awards/listoffellows_year.cfm|title=Awards & Scholarships - MSA Fellows by Election Year }}</ref> and of the Microanalysis society in 2022.{{r|MASFellows}}
She is also a fellow of the [[Meteoritical Society]].{{r|mas|metsoc}} Asteroid [[8468 Rhondastroud]] was named after her in 2012.{{r|sbdb|asteroid}}
